text:
incident-bot: Paging @tara-oncall (sev-2) — AtlasCorp (VPC-dedicated) observed elevated token error rate and increased 5xx from model route. Impact: subset of tenant traffic (10%) returning garbled tokens. See metrics: https://obs.redwood/atlas/streams

anna-sre: I can see a spike starting 09:12 UTC, 4x error rate. Requests are still completing but outputs are corrupted, not timeouts.

mike-eng: That matches a model variant regression after the last canary push to the dedicated pool. Likely KV cache/quant mismatch.

alice-cs: Atlas on the line. They're seeing customer-facing hallucinations in billing summaries. Want immediate mitigation, legal is asking for isolation.

pete-runtime: Quick check: the serving logs show mixed quantized runtimes between gptx-1.3-q and gptx-1.2-safe on same shard. Looking like a routing mismatch when fallback kicked in.

tara-oncall: Ok. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pin Atlas tenant to the stable variant (gptx-1.2-safe) 2) Disable cross-variant fallback on their pool 3) Notify Atlas customer SRE about the change. I'll take lead.

anna-sre: +1. I'll do the pin and override routing. Pete help me validate the conf.

pete-runtime: On it. Suggested routing override snippet:

```
# tenant routing override
{"tenant_id": "atlas", "pool": "dedicated-eu-3", "route": {"model": "gptx-1.2-safe", "pin": true, "disable_fallback": true}}
```

mike-eng: Note: ensure KV cache flush after pin to avoid stale context merging across quant variants. Command to run on shard manager: `shardctl flush-kv --tenant atlas --pool dedicated-eu-3`

tara-oncall: I'll run the override now and perform a canary test (10 reqs). Anna, please coordinate with Alice to tell Atlas.

anna-sre: Running route override: `infra-cli routes apply --file atlas-pin.json` (applying).

ops-bot: Deployed route override to dedicated-eu-3 for tenant atlas. change_id=chg_20260315_001

pete-runtime: kv flush queued. Running: `shardctl flush-kv --tenant atlas --pool dedicated-eu-3`

pete-runtime: KV flush completed, 0 errors.

mike-eng: Canary tests (10 reqs) -> 10/10 returned expected structure, token streams look normal. Latency unchanged.

alice-cs: Telling Atlas: "We've pinned your workspace to a stable model variant and disabled fallback while we investigate. Expect no functional regression; ops will follow up with a postmortem." They asked for ETA on rollback steps if they see anything else.

tara-oncall: Good. Next: follow-up investigation — capture the canary logs, compare kernel selection paths for gptx-1.3-q vs gptx-1.2-safe. Pete, Mike, please own a short RCA. I'll run the incident timeline and hand off to morning on-call at 12:00 UTC.

pete-runtime: Will gather kernel traces and serving traces for the shard. Suspect a recent kernel change in the q-quant path.

mike-eng: I'll reproduce in staging with a replay of Atlas request traces and run with the canary gptx-1.3-q to surface the mismatch.

anna-sre: Logging timeline in the incident doc: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/atlas-2026-pin-protect (note: doc created).

tara-oncall: Handoff notes for morning: tenant pinned to gptx-1.2-safe, fallback disabled, change_id=chg_20260315_001, KV flushed, canary passed. Severity reduced to sev-3 for now. Please monitor token error rate and hallucination reports for next 24h.

alice-cs: Atlas acknowledged and requested a postmortem. They want a timeline and whether their tokens were exposed. We're clear on data isolation — only routing change applied, no data copy. I'll handle comms.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to sev-3 by tara-oncall.

tara-oncall: Assigning owners: RCA = mike-eng, kernel traces = pete-runtime, customer comms = alice-cs, long-term mitigation (routing hardening) = anna-sre. Tagging @eng-ml for quant path review.

mike-eng: I'll drop initial findings into the doc by 11:00 UTC. If we find a kernel regression, schedule an emergency patch and a staged rollout plan.

pete-runtime: Adding artifact links once traces are uploaded.

anna-sre: Thanks team. I'll post a short status update to Atlas and to #incidents in 10m.

alice-cs: TL;DR for Atlas: pinned to stable variant, disabled auto-fallback, KV flush performed, monitoring in place.

tara-oncall: Ok handing off to morning oncall at 12:00 UTC — if anything regresses, escalate back to sev-2 and page the oncall rotation.

incident-bot: Handoff complete. New oncall: tom-oncall (12:00 UTC).
